outputs.L2:
An electric drive device includes a motor housing that contains an electric motor. A heat-dissipating base member is secured to the end face of the motor housing located on the side opposite the output-shaft portion of the motor’s rotating shaft, and this base member extends in the axial direction away from the output-shaft portion.  

The device also includes two electronic control units forming a redundant system. One electronic control unit is positioned along the direction in which the heat-dissipating base member extends and has a circuit board thermally conductively fixed to the heat-dissipating base member, allowing heat to be transferred to it. The other electronic control unit is likewise arranged along the extension direction of the heat-dissipating base member and includes a circuit board fixed to the heat-dissipating base member in a thermally conductive manner.  

The circuit boards of both electronic control units are attached to the heat-dissipating base member while being inclined relative to the direction in which the base member extends.
outputs.L3:
The electric drive device includes a motor housing that accommodates an electric motor. A heat radiation base body is fixed to an end surface of the motor housing on the side opposite to the output shaft side of the electric motor. This heat radiation base body functions as a support member and also as a heat-dissipating member for electronic components.

Two redundant electronic control units are provided on the heat radiation base body. These electronic control units are arranged along the direction in which the heat radiation base body extends, so that the device can achieve redundancy while maintaining a compact configuration.

Each electronic control unit includes a board on which control components are mounted. The board of each electronic control unit is fixed to the heat radiation base body in a manner that allows heat generated by the board or its mounted components to be conducted to the heat radiation base body. As a result, heat can be efficiently transferred from the electronic control units to the heat radiation base body and then dissipated.

The boards of the two electronic control units are mounted at a slant with respect to the extension direction of the heat radiation base body. By arranging the boards in this inclined orientation, the electronic control units can be efficiently positioned along the heat radiation base body while contributing to improved space utilization, heat dissipation, and overall compactness of the electric drive device.
outputs.L4:
An electric drive device includes an electric motor and a control unit integrated with the motor. The motor has a motor housing and an output shaft projecting from one side of the housing. On the side opposite the output shaft, a heat-radiation base body is provided so as to extend from the motor housing. This heat-radiation base body serves as both a structural support for electronic components and a heat-dissipating member for releasing heat generated during operation.

A plurality of electronic control units are mounted on the heat-radiation base body. The electronic control units may be provided redundantly, for example as a first control system and a second control system, so that the electric drive device can continue operating even if one control system fails. Each electronic control unit includes a circuit board on which electronic components such as power switching elements, control circuits, sensors, and connectors may be mounted. The circuit boards are fixed to the heat-radiation base body in a manner that allows heat generated by the electronic components to be efficiently transferred to the base body.

The circuit boards are arranged at an inclined or slanted angle with respect to the direction in which the heat-radiation base body extends from the motor housing. In other words, the boards are not simply placed parallel to the extension direction of the base body, but are positioned obliquely. This angled arrangement makes it possible to secure sufficient mounting area for the electronic components while reducing the overall axial length or radial size of the device. As a result, the redundant control units can be housed in a compact space adjacent to the motor.

Because the circuit boards are thermally connected to the heat-radiation base body, heat produced by the electronic components is efficiently conducted away from the boards. The heat-radiation base body then releases the heat to the surrounding environment and may also transfer heat to the motor housing. This configuration improves cooling performance without requiring a large separate heat sink or a complex cooling structure.

By integrating the redundant electronic control units with the motor in this manner, the electric drive device achieves both reliability and compactness. The redundant control structure enhances operational safety, while the slanted board arrangement and thermal connection to the heat-radiation base body contribute to improved heat dissipation and efficient use of space. Such a configuration is particularly suitable for applications requiring high reliability, limited installation space, and stable motor control performance.
outputs.L5:
# Boards

Boards are essential tools used in many areas of life, from education and business to construction, design, and technology. A board can be a physical surface, such as a whiteboard, notice board, or wooden board, or it can refer to a group of people responsible for making decisions, such as a board of directors.

In schools and offices, boards help people share information clearly. Whiteboards and blackboards are commonly used for teaching, brainstorming, and planning. Notice boards are useful for displaying announcements, schedules, and important updates. In creative environments, mood boards and vision boards help organize ideas, images, colors, and goals in a visual way.

In business, boards play a major role in leadership and strategy. A board of directors guides an organization, makes important decisions, and ensures that the company is moving in the right direction. These boards often discuss financial performance, long-term goals, risks, and policies.

Boards are also widely used in construction and manufacturing. Wooden boards, circuit boards, and fiber boards each serve different purposes. For example, circuit boards are found in electronic devices and allow components to connect and function properly.

Overall, boards are practical, versatile, and important. Whether used for communication, organization, creativity, building, or leadership, boards help people structure ideas, make decisions, and complete tasks more effectively.

counterfactuals.prompt: Rewrite the following patent claim in plain English while keeping the technical terminology: an electric drive device with a motor housing, heat radiation base body, and two redundant electronic control units mounted on slanted boards.
counterfactuals.output:
An electric drive device includes:

- a **motor housing**;
- a **heat radiation base body** attached to or integrated with the motor housing; and
- two **redundant electronic control units**.

Each electronic control unit is mounted on a respective **slanted board**, and the boards are arranged at an angle relative to the heat radiation base body or motor housing so that the control units can be installed in a compact layout while allowing heat to be transferred to the heat radiation base body.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the invention from a Japanese patent abstract about an electric motor drive device having a heat radiation base body attached opposite the output shaft and two redundant control units mounted along it.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is an electric motor drive device designed to be compact, reliable, and thermally efficient.

It has a heat-radiating base body attached to the motor on the side opposite the output shaft. Two independent/redundant control units for driving the motor are mounted along this heat-radiating base. Each control unit includes drive/control components, such as power elements, and is arranged so that heat generated during operation is efficiently transferred to and dissipated through the base body.

By placing the two control units along the common heat-radiation base on the non-output side of the motor, the device can maintain redundancy—allowing continued operation even if one control system fails—while reducing size and improving cooling performance. This structure is especially useful for applications requiring high reliability, such as electric power steering or other vehicle motor systems.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft an abstract for a patent claim describing a motor housing, a heat dissipation base extending opposite the output shaft, and two redundant electronic control units with boards slanted and thermally connected to the base.
counterfactuals.output:
**Abstract**

A motor assembly includes a motor housing supporting a motor having an output shaft extending from a first side of the housing. A heat dissipation base is coupled to, or formed integrally with, the housing and extends from an opposite second side of the housing in a direction away from the output shaft. First and second electronic control units are arranged in the heat dissipation base to provide redundant control of the motor. Each electronic control unit includes a circuit board carrying control electronics. The circuit boards are disposed at an inclined orientation relative to a longitudinal axis of the motor and are thermally coupled to the heat dissipation base, such as through thermally conductive supports, pads, or direct contact portions. Heat generated by the control electronics is conducted from the inclined circuit boards to the heat dissipation base and dissipated away from the motor housing, while the redundant electronic control units enable continued operation upon failure of one control unit.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
